scenes.headline: How a rubric turns a board memo into a reward
scenes.sub: Reinforcement learning on work that has no unit tests
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lapis! Code has unit tests. A board memo does not. So how does Ultramarine get a reward out of one?

scenes.text: Write each task's grade as weighted propositions. A judge marks each one met or unmet, and the weighted sum becomes the reward.
scenes.say: Write the grade as weighted propositions. A judge marks each one met or unmet, and the weighted sum is the reward.

left.title: Verifiable RL
left.say: In coding, a test decides, and it is hard to fool.

right.title: Rubric RL
right.say: Here a judge reads each criterion, errors carry negative weight, and the grader sits out of the policy's reach.

steps.say: A generator builds a task, its world and its rubric, from eighty-eight kinds of professional work.
The policy works in the Feather harness, with its loop outside the sandbox.
It edits a real Office file. The judge reads it as text and marks every criterion.
Rewards are compared with their group's mean, and one update nudges the adapter toward the better attempts.
Six answers. Three are complete, three give one piece each.
An overfit criterion rejects valid answers. A vague one accepts incomplete ones.
Their criterion states the real condition, and matches the boundary.

parts.say: Add the weights of every criterion judged met. Error criteria are negative, so they subtract.

parts.note: the most a perfect memo can earn
parts.say: Divide by the total positive weight. A memo with every number right can still score only two thirds.

scenes.label: points gained over the base, on all six knowledge-work benchmarks
scenes.say: The result: about four points over the base on all six knowledge-work benchmarks, slightly worse on coding.

scenes.label: Fable 5 at max reasoning, per task, over Ultramarine
scenes.note: a price ratio on their own benchmark
scenes.say: Sixty-three times cheaper per task than Fable 5 at max. A price ratio, on their own benchmark, with the scores split four and four.

scenes.text: Without tests, the reward is only as good as the boundary each criterion draws.
scenes.say: Without tests, the reward is only as good as each criterion's boundary.

recap: Weighted propositions, judged met or unmet
Grader walled off from the policy
Gains where it trained, weights not out yet
scenes.say: Weighted propositions, a walled-off grader, gains where it trained. Weights still to come.
